cases.name: NIH Case: Cardiomegaly
cases.impression:
1. Moderate cardiomegaly with a cardiothoracic ratio of 0.529, consistent with known congestive heart failure.
2. No acute pulmonary edema, focal airspace disease, or pleural effusion.
cases.dictation_transcript: In this 68-year-old female presenting with progressive dyspnea on exertion and orthopnea, the frontal chest radiograph demonstrates borderline cardiomegaly with a cardiothoracic ratio of 0.529, localized primarily to the left heart border. The lungs remain clear without overt alveolar pulmonary edema or pleural effusions. Clinical correlation with volume status, biomarkers, and management of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction is recommended.
cases.recommendations:
1. Assess volume status, serum NT-proBNP, and electrolytes per ACC/AHA guidelines.
2. Obtain formal 2D echocardiography to evaluate current ventricular ejection fraction and wall motion.

cases.name: Clinical Case: Pulmonary Nodule & Mass
cases.impression: 1. Thoracic nodule and mass located in the left mid zone, highly indeterminate for primary bronchogenic neoplasm given patient age, 35 pack-year smoking history, unintentional weight loss, and hemoptysis. 2. Bilateral interstitial infiltrates, which may reflect inflammatory changes, aspiration, or secondary post-obstructive phenomena. 3. Mild cardiomegaly with a cardiothoracic ratio of 0.559.
cases.dictation_transcript: This is a 64-year-old male presenting with chronic cough, 14-pound weight loss, and hemoptysis, evaluated with a frontal chest radiograph. Automated deep learning and visual analysis demonstrate a left mid-zone pulmonary nodule scoring 70.6 percent and a distinct mass scoring 65.8 percent, accompanied by bilateral infiltrates and a cardiothoracic ratio of 0.559 indicating mild cardiomegaly. Given the strong smoking history and hemoptysis, these findings mandate urgent dedicated contrast-enhanced chest CT for tissue characterization and pulmonary oncology consultation.
cases.recommendations: 1. Perform a dedicated contrast-enhanced thin-slice chest CT without delay per Fleischner Society and ACCP guidelines to further characterize the left lung nodule and mass and assess mediastinal lymphadenopathy. 2. Urgent pulmonology and thoracic oncology referral for possible bronchoscopy or image-guided tissue biopsy. 3. Sputum cytology and infectious workup to rule out concomitant infection.

cases.name: NIH Case: Thoracic Mass & Consolidation
cases.impression:
1. Indeterminate left mid-zone pulmonary nodule/mass (model score 0.74), requiring further diagnostic evaluation.
2. Subacute right chest discomfort and evening fevers in the setting of a focal pulmonary lesion, warranting urgent evaluation for infectious, inflammatory, or neoplastic etiologies.
3. Normal cardiothoracic ratio and clear pleural spaces without acute cardiopulmonary decompensation.
cases.dictation_transcript: This is an urgent evaluation of a 58-year-old female presenting with subacute chest discomfort and evening fevers. Frontal chest radiograph demonstrates a focal indeterminate pulmonary nodule in the left mid-zone, corroborated by deep learning predictions with a 74.2 percent confidence score. The cardiothoracic ratio is normal at 0.381, and the pleural spaces are clear. Given the constitutional symptoms and focal parenchymal lesion, an urgent contrast-enhanced chest CT is recommended to definitively characterize this abnormality and guide further clinical management.
cases.recommendations:
1. Urgent dedicated contrast-enhanced thin-slice chest CT per Fleischner Society guidelines for detailed morphological risk stratification.
2. Correlation with complete blood count, inflammatory markers (ESR/CRP), and clinical infectious workup given evening fevers.
3. Outpatient pulmonology referral for consideration of image-guided biopsy or PET/CT depending on CT findings.

cases.name: Clinical Case: Atelectasis & Fibrosis
cases.ctr_status: Normal for AP Portable (<0.55; AP magnification adjusted)
cases.impression: 1. Right mid-zone subsegmental atelectasis, secondary to post-operative shallow breathing and underlying interstitial lung disease. 2. No acute focal consolidation, large pleural effusion, or pneumothorax.
cases.dictation_transcript: This is an AP portable chest radiograph on a 71-year-old male status-post surgery with mild hypoxemia. Evaluation demonstrates right mid-zone subsegmental atelectasis corresponding to shallow inspiration, alongside stable interstitial lung disease features and a normal cardiothoracic ratio of 0.536. There is no evidence of acute pulmonary edema, focal airspace consolidation, or pneumothorax. Clinical correlation with incentive spirometry and aggressive pulmonary hygiene is recommended.
cases.recommendations: 1. Encourage incentive spirometry, early ambulation, and deep breathing exercises to treat subsegmental atelectasis (Fleischner Society guidelines). 2. Serial chest radiography if clinical respiratory status deteriorates.

cases.name: Clinical Case: Acute Pneumonia & Infiltration
cases.impression: 1. Left mid lung zone pulmonary infiltration (score 51.9%), highly suspicious for acute infectious pneumonia given clinical presentation. 2. No pleural effusion or cardiomegaly (CTR 0.452).
cases.dictation_transcript: This is a 72-year-old male evaluated in the emergency department for high fever and purulent cough. Frontal chest radiograph demonstrates focal pulmonary infiltration localized to the left mid lung zone by Grad-CAM analysis, with a normal cardiothoracic ratio of 0.452. The pleural spaces are clear bilaterally. Clinical correlation with sputum cultures and initiation of empiric antimicrobial therapy per ATS/IDSA guidelines are strongly recommended.
cases.recommendations: 1. Initiate empiric antimicrobial therapy following ATS/IDSA guidelines for patients with comorbidities. 2. Obtain complete blood count, blood cultures, and sputum Gram stain/culture. 3. Perform follow-up chest radiograph in 4 to 6 weeks to document complete radiographic resolution.

cases.name: Normal Baseline Control

cases.dictation_transcript: I reviewed the frontal chest radiograph for this forty-five-year-old female presenting for routine preoperative cardiopulmonary clearance. The lungs are clear bilaterally with no focal consolidation or suspicious nodule, and the cardiomediastinal silhouette is within normal limits. There is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Overall, this represents a normal chest radiograph suitable for routine outpatient clearance.
